'''Óscar José Torres Martínez''' (born December 18, 1976) is a Venezuelan former professional [[basketball]] player. A 6'6" native of [[Caracas]], Torres played at the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions.

==Professional career==
Torres became the first Venezuelan-born player in [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) history, when he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]], for the [[2001–02 NBA season]]. Torres averaged 6.0 points over the course of the season, and scored an NBA career-high 28 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], on December 11, 2001. He spent the next season with the [[Golden State Warriors]], and averaged 3.1 points per game.

Torres led the [[Russia]]n team [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow Region]] to the 2006 [[Eurocup Basketball|EuroCup]] finals, before losing to [[DKV Joventut]]. Torres was transferred [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], from Khimki, in February 2007, and with them, he won the [[Russian Professional Basketball Championship|Russian Championship]] and the [[Russian Basketball Cup|Russian Cup]].

He was released from CSKA in June that year. On August 21, 2007, he signed with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] team [[Fortitudo Bologna|Climamio Bologna]].<ref>[http://195.56.77.208/news/?id=83786&redi= Torres signs with Fortitudo.]</ref>

==National team career==
Torres also played with the senior [[Venezuelan national basketball team]] at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship|2002]] and [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006]] editions of the [[FIBA World Cup]]s.
